title: Measured memory montage
intent: Build a compact, reviewable recollection from scene evidence while preserving live sound and creative alternatives.
applicability: One or more video sources contain distinct visual beats
Chronology or thematic evidence can order candidate regions
contraindications: A single uninterrupted performance must remain continuous
Source rights do not permit derivative editing
rules: Keep picture and selected live sound synchronized
Offer multiple executable structures for divergent creative intent
heuristics: Use chronological order when semantic evidence is absent
Prefer duplicate-free regions when duplicate evidence exists
constraints: Scene-change score is not a semantic claim
Optional thematic ranking cannot silently become cut authority
qc: Check loudness across live sound and music
positive_examples: Several home-video scenes assembled into concise chronological beats
A sparse montage retaining selected ambient sound
negative_examples: A continuous speech where visual scene scores create arbitrary cuts
A music-driven cut using unlicensed audio
promotion_questions: Which local embeddings best support privacy-preserving thematic grouping?
How should emotional structure be evaluated without pretending to objective truth?
Which beat detector transfers across music genres?
